judged_text: The computed index keys `[z.string().toString()]` / `[z.string().optional().toString()]` do not create a catch-all index signature — they evaluate to a single static string key at module load, so the comment 'Assume that any property with a number is the expiry' describes behavior the schema does not implement. In sync mode the parsed data contains only access_token (plus one junk literal key); every other property (expiry, scope, instance_url for salesforce) is silently stripped, so callers relying on those fields in `tokenResponse.data` get undefined and the schema's advertised permissiveness is an illusion.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, `minimumTokenResponseSchema` uses computed keys `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]`. In a JS object literal those expressions are evaluated immediately to a single concrete string key (e.g., a ZodString’s `toString()`), not a wildcard/index signature. Zod will therefore not accept/retain arbitrary keys like `expiry_date`, and (worse) the required numeric computed key will almost never exist in real token responses, making `safeParse` fail in “sync mode”. This directly contradicts the comments and breaks the intended permissive parsing behavior.
